repository_context.workstream: XRP intelligence and research-only corporate relationship evidence

source_policy.preferred: Primary issuer, corporate, counterparty and SEC filings.
source_policy.interpretation: A company announcement establishes what that company announced. It does not independently prove realized throughput, market share, token demand, collateral use, customer balances or economic impact.

sbic.legal_basis: Act on the Small and Medium Business Investment and Consultation Company, Act No. 101 of 1963, Article 2: https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/338AC0000000101
sbic.relationship: Three separate regional statutory investment companies that identify one another as sister companies. They are not SBI Holdings, Inc. and the reviewed official profiles do not establish that they are SBI Holdings subsidiaries.
sbic.related_name_collision: SBI CAPITAL Co., Ltd. appears as a separate SBI Holdings entity in a historical SBI report; its current 2026 legal status remains unresolved. Do not merge that entity with the three regional SBIC companies.
sbic.chatgpt_context: Tokyo SBIC East's official 2025-06-12 to 2025-06-13 training for investee companies included ChatGPT usage and Microsoft Copilot functions. This is educational use by an SBIC company, not an OpenAI partnership.

ask_coin.evidence: Permission documentation describes ASK on Base and Polygon, including OFT/Stargate-related functionality.
ask_coin.warning: Do not assert this is the intended ASK Coin without the original context.

actual_capital.warning: Do not conflate the phrase with the SBI presentation's 'Actual XRP' category. That category is described as Ripple holdings currently not in circulation, not cash, actual capital or a verified capital-flow measure.

sbic_chatgpt.evidence: The SBIC East training course included ChatGPT and Copilot. No OpenAI/SBIC partnership was established.

facts: SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank each disclosed a $25 million Circle share purchase at Circle's June 2025 NYSE listing, $50 million combined.
SBI Holdings and Circle's group company agreed in March 2025 to form SBI Circle Holdings; the JV was subsequently established.
SBI VC Trade began public USDC distribution in Japan in March 2025.
caveats: The $50 million is a historical investment amount, not current market value or current ownership percentage.
No XRP demand, XRP collateral or XRPL transaction volume is implied.

facts: SBI Holdings disclosed on 2026-05-12 that a consolidated subsidiary participated in Circle's ARC Token presale; Circle described a $222 million investor consortium. SBI's own allocation was not disclosed.
Circle's 2026-09-16 Arc mainnet announcement lists SBI Group among founding validators and quotes SBI CEO Yoshitaka Kitao describing SBI's role in Arc operation and governance.
Circle's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q recognizes $181.8 million of ARC token presale revenue during Q3 and the nine-month period.
caveats: ARC is Arc's native token, not XRP.
Arc is Circle's separate EVM-compatible Layer 1, not XRPL.
SBI's presale amount, current ARC holdings and validator rewards were not disclosed in these sources.

facts: SBI disclosed a 2016 Ripple investment and formed SBI Ripple Asia as a joint venture.
SBI's 2025 disclosures described Ripple as an investee and referenced a roughly 9% stake at the relevant historical disclosure date.
caveats: Current post-2025 Ripple ownership percentage has not been independently recalculated from a current cap table.
A Ripple equity stake and SBI Ripple Asia do not prove SBI or its customers hold XRP or use XRP as collateral.

facts: SBI VC Trade announced RLUSD handling in Japan on 2026-06-24; launch support was Ethereum-only in the cited product notice.

SBI Group and Startale launched trust-type yen stablecoin JPYSC on 2026-06-24. SBI Shinsei Trust is issuer and SBI VC Trade distributes it; initial availability was restricted to SBI VC Trade accounts.
SBI said public-chain circulation would follow once legal and tax practices were clarified.
caveats: An Ethereum-only RLUSD listing is not XRPL distribution.
JPYSC's initial account-limited availability is not proof of public-chain circulation or XRP use.
Neither announcement proves XRP is required collateral.

facts: SBI disclosures describe a 51.69% SBI Coinhako ownership position and a strategic plan involving JPYSC, USDC and RLUSD for yen-dollar and cross-border settlement.
caveats: Strategy language is not evidence of live material settlement, XRP demand or measured token flows.

facts: On 2026-10-30 SBI Holdings and SMFG announced a capital and business alliance to jointly examine financial services using stablecoins and other tokenized assets.
caveats: The release describes joint study and development; it is not proof of a production XRP rail or XRP-token use.

facts: SBI announced a 2026-11-13 MOU concerning stablecoin-based remittance exploration with Cambodia-related counterparties and SBI group entities.
caveats: No XRP settlement or production throughput was established by the MOU.

facts: SBI and Startale joined the Open Standard initiative in October 2026; the consortium included Coinbase among 140+ members and discussed JPYSC/OUSD interoperability.
caveats: Consortium co-membership is not a bilateral SBI-Coinbase partnership and does not establish XRP demand.

facts: Circle's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q says Coinbase receives allocations based on USDC held on Coinbase's platform after issuer retention, plus half of the remaining ecosystem-growth payment base after approved third-party participant payments.
Circle reported $331.3 million of distribution costs under its Coinbase agreements in Q3 2026 and $986.6 million for the first nine months of 2026.

Circle reported total distribution and transaction costs of $409.169 million in Q3 and $1,224.985 million for nine months. Derived Coinbase concentration is approximately 81.0% in Q3 and 80.5% year to date.
Coinbase's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q says the Circle arrangement was renewed on the same terms and average USDC held in Coinbase products reached $22 billion.
caveats: These are Circle distribution expenses, not a direct measure of Coinbase net profit or USDC reserve income.
Coinbase's $22 billion average USDC balance is a platform balance measure, not XRP liquidity or XRP collateral.
The 81.0% and 80.5% figures are calculations from the same Circle filing, not a separately reported ratio.

facts: Coinbase and Ripple announced RLUSD availability across Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and the retail app on 2026-10-28.
At launch, RLUSD deposits and withdrawals were supported on XRPL, Base and Ethereum.
Coinbase Global Exchange availability and RLUSD collateral functionality were described as following later, not live at launch.
caveats: Listing on XRPL does not establish net XRPL inflows or XRP-token demand.
Future collateral plans are not evidence of live XRP collateral use.
No public launch balance, flow or collateral utilization was identified in these announcements.

facts: Ripple and BNY announced on 2026-10-27 that BNY supports XRP and RLUSD on its Digital Asset Custody platform.
BNY is identified as primary reserve custodian for RLUSD and has a custody relationship with Ripple Prime.
BNY and Ripple described future direct RLUSD mint/redeem through BNY and tokenized trade-finance work on XRPL, subject to client requirements and final regulatory approvals.
caveats: Custody availability is not evidence of actual customer holdings or AUC for XRP.
Future mint/redeem and tokenized trade-finance plans are not current production flows.
The announcement does not state XRP is the settlement asset or collateral for the proposed C2FO workflow.

facts: Circle and DBS announced on 2026-11-18 that eligible institutional clients can directly mint and redeem USDC through DBS with 24/7 USD-USDC settlement.
Both organizations participate in Project BLOOM, led by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
caveats: This is a USDC banking/payment rail, not an XRP or XRPL partnership.
The announcement does not disclose realized transaction volume.

facts: Paribu was an Arc day-one launch partner and supports USDC deposits/withdrawals over Arc; Paribu Custody added Arc support.
Circle and Paribu signed a 2026-11-24 MOU to explore Arc products, tokenization, institutional custody, education and research.
caveats: The MOU is exploratory; no committed volume or production use case was disclosed.
Arc is Circle's separate network, not XRPL.

facts: Ripple's 2026-10-28 release reported a $900 million annualized product-revenue run rate, more than $16 trillion in transactions enabled across Ripple products during 2025, more than 85 licenses, 1,700+ institutional/corporate/enterprise users, 60+ payout markets, and nearly $150 billion of lifetime Ripple Payments volume by year-end.
The same release described RLUSD at approximately $2.6 billion market capitalization and said it was used across Ripple products.
caveats: These are Ripple's company-reported metrics across products, not XRP-only volume, XRP sales, XRP liquidity, or XRPL settlement volume.
No independent product-level bridge from Ripple Payments volume to XRP-token usage was provided in the release.

cross_hypotheses_and_disconfirming_evide: Corporate partnerships, custody support, exchange listings, stablecoin circulation, and tokenized-asset plans do not automatically create XRP demand.
Circle Arc is a separate EVM-compatible L1; SBI Group's Arc validator/presale activity is not evidence of XRP or XRPL use.
RLUSD being available on XRPL, Base and Ethereum does not establish net XRPL inflows, XRP bridge demand, or XRP collateral use.
BNY custody support establishes product availability, not balances held, AUC, transfer volume, or collateral utilization.
Coinbase Global Exchange RLUSD collateral functionality was described as future at the 2026-10-28 launch.
Ripple's $16T transaction figure and $900M annualized product revenue are company-reported cross-product metrics, not XRP-only financial metrics.
SBI's JPYSC, USDC and RLUSD strategy is a multi-stablecoin strategy; no measured XRP settlement requirement was disclosed.
SBI and SMBC's October 2026 alliance is exploratory; it does not establish a live production rail.
The direct Circle-Coinbase distribution relationship is financially material, but it is a USDC reserve/distribution relationship, not an XRP market-flow signal.
unresolved_questions: Current post-2025 SBI Ripple equity percentage and voting/economic rights.
Current Coinbase ownership percentage in Circle after IPO, subsequent transactions and Q3 2026 disclosures.
Product-level split of Ripple's reported payment volume attributable to XRP versus fiat/stablecoin or other rails.
Actual XRP balances, flows, custody AUC and collateral utilization at Coinbase, BNY, SBI VC Trade and other institutions.
Whether any RLUSD Coinbase collateral feature went live after the October 28 launch announcement, and actual utilization if so.
Independent raw-byte capture and point-in-time receipt linkage for each primary-source event.

provenance.source_independence: Counterparty pairs were used where available (SBI/Circle, Coinbase/Ripple, Ripple/BNY, Circle/DBS, Circle/Paribu). These are independent publisher records of announcements, but they are not independent measurements of realized flows.
provenance.disagreements: Company claims and future plans are preserved separately from realized balance, flow, custody and collateral evidence.
